missed_mechanisms.evidence: grep -rn "was_duplicate" crates --include=*.rs returns hits ONLY inside crates/adaptive-transport/src/receiver.rs (field decl :71-72, set at :229). The product server ignores it: crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:2146-2156 only reads `out.delivered` and `out.ack`. crates/client-core/src/runtime.rs:533-580 ServerStats has no duplicate counter. §9.4's stated purpose ('Bu, spurious retransmit'i sender'a bildirir', specs/adaptive-transport-engine-spec.md:700-701) therefore has no product observability path.

missed_mechanisms.name: RecoverFwd transition destroys the ARQ backlog and resets ARQ_RETX_CAP accounting
missed_mechanisms.evidence: crates/adaptive-transport/src/sender.rs:5514 `let recs: Vec<LostRec> = self.pending_lost.drain(..).collect();` — entering plan_forward_duplication drains the ENTIRE pending_lost. DupRec (sender.rs:1313-1321) carries no retx_count, and crates/adaptive-transport/src/sender.rs:5634 emits copies with `self.track_sent(dup.unit, now_ns, 0, TransmitKind::Duplicate)` — retx_count 0. A Duplicate-origin loss then never re-enters pending_lost (sender.rs:3318 `if p.origin != TransmitKind::Duplicate {` gates the push at :3340-3345). Net effect: any transient ack_confidence dip converts the ARQ queue into fire-once copies and erases per-unit retransmit history, so §9.1's ARQ_RETX_CAP is not a per-unit lifetime bound.
missed_mechanisms.suggested_classification: SHIP with an unrecorded semantic gap — belongs in the §9.1 cap record as a caveat, and is a candidate spec-amendment item

corrected_classifications.reason: DELETE is not defensible. The guard is normative in specs/adaptive-transport-engine-spec.md:679 and is recorded by the spec itself at :1081 as a 'sözleşme-notu' (contract note) — an acknowledged defense-in-depth branch, not obsolete code. It is also genuinely reachable: FuzzyConfig::validate (crates/adaptive-transport/src/fusion.rs:298-311) bounds consequents only from above (`if v > PERMILLE`), so arq_light: 0 validates, and Sender::try_with_fuzzy_config (sender.rs:1771) is public. It is wired (its only consumer is the product path at sender.rs:5328) and exercised (tv_arq.rs:106). Inert-under-default-config is the same status as a bounds check, not death. Removing it would require amending §9 and would reopen the K-1 arq=0 degeneracy class.

Classification stands but the record understates the gap and misstates the impl. The finding says budget_cfg is 'used for send_rate_final 4034 and parity clamp'; there is no parity clamp — budget::budget_cap_permille and budget::parity_final have zero callers workspace-wide (budget.rs:38, :45), and the sole budget:: call is sender.rs:4032 send_rate_final with cap = u64::MAX. The correct scope is: the whole §8.5 available_redundancy_budget mechanism (parity clamp + BtlBw-derived send-rate cap) is disconnected, of which duplication is one leg.
